newsitem.title: UK: Moorfield says Greycoat unwilling to talk.
newsitem.headline: Moorfield says Greycoat unwilling to talk.

text.p: British property group Moorfield Estates Plc, leading an attempt to split up larger rival Greycoat Plc with the backing of some rebel Greycoat shareholders, said on Monday that talks between the two firms to find a negotiatied way forward were not progressing.

In a statement, Moorfield said it had been informed today by Greycoat that it "is currently unwilling to enter into any meaningful dialogue which will enable the detailed proposal made by Moorfield to advance".
In the light of what it called Greycoat's "obduracy", Moorfield would continue talks with "certain shareholders".

Moorfield on Friday asked Greycoat to provide it with some details on "issues of material concern," so that it could attempt to proceed with its merger proposal and demonstrate that value would be created for both companies.
An extraordinary meeting to vote on a resolution to change Greycoat completely is due to reconvene at noon on Thursday.

In today's statement Moorfield, which is smaller than Greycoat, said it was not suggesting full-scale due diligence "but rather requires clarification and comfort on a number of issues which could be dealt with in one day's cooperative discusssion."
According to rebel shareholder Brian Myerson, who has led the assault on the current Greycoat board, the firm should be forced to sit down and talk to Moorfield.
He has said he believes holders of about 40 percent of Greycoat shares back the Moorfield plans.
